title: Structured Windows UI Automation InvokePattern actuation with approval binding and stale-target revalidation
objective: Establish the first narrow COTRA-P09 structured actuation grain on top of the SG-000027 read-only observation registry, the SG-000018 replay-resistant foundation, SG-000019 class enforcement, SG-000020 trust and revoke records, and the closed COTRA-P08 registry: a single approved InvokePattern actuation shape bound to server-derived process identity, typed window identity, typed element identity, expected tree generation, expected control type, expected Invoke pattern support, expected enabled state, workspace scope, and policy revision, with fresh SOFT approval digest binding, immediate pre-actuation stale-target revalidation, protected Cotra approval-surface exclusion, and explicit denial of every other actuation, coordinate, synthetic-input, screenshot, clipboard, network, and elevation shape.

include: single new actuation shape uia.element/invoke bound to one server-allocated typed element identity with arguments element_id, expected_tree_generation, and expected_control_type only

server-derived process identity binding PID, executable digest, process creation generation, session identity, workspace scope, and policy revision, with PID reuse and restart fail-closed at actuation time

typed window identity binding owning process, window handle, process generation, window generation, session and desktop identity, workspace scope, and policy revision, with destroyed, replaced, and reused-handle fail-closed at actuation time

typed element identity binding owning window, UIA runtime identity, tree snapshot generation, expected control type, supported patterns, workspace scope, and policy revision, with disappeared, replaced, role-changed, generation-changed, and policy-drifted fail-closed

Invoke eligibility allowlist limited to Button, Hyperlink, MenuItem, and SplitButton control types with required Invoke pattern support and required enabled state, with all other control types, unsupported patterns, and disabled elements denied

fresh per-action SOFT approval with one-shot exact-digest binding over workspace, policy revision, process identity, process generation, window identity, window generation, element identity, tree generation, control type, and action material, with nonce, expiry, one-shot consumption, and stale-digest fail-closed

immediate pre-actuation revalidation of process liveness, executable identity, process generation, window existence, HWND ownership by the expected process, element existence, runtime identity, tree generation, control type, pattern support, enabled state, protected-surface status, workspace binding, and policy revision, with any drift denied without silent retargeting

protected Cotra approval and security surface exclusion so invoke can never target approval dialogs, STRONG presence surfaces, workspace trust controls, emergency revoke, or security-sensitive Cotra UI, failing closed on uncertainty
explicit denial of coordinate fallback, mouse fallback, keyboard fallback, SendInput fallback, click-as-invoke, and silent escalation when InvokePattern is unsupported or the target is stale

deterministic unit and security tests for happy-path invoke, stale process, restarted process, PID reuse, stale HWND, reused HWND, wrong process and window pairing, stale element, wrong runtime identity, wrong tree generation, changed control type, unsupported pattern, disabled element, protected Cotra surface, password and secret element, missing approval, stale approval, reused approval, incorrect approval digest, policy drift, state drift, caller-supplied PID, caller-supplied HWND, caller-supplied runtime id, selector, coordinate fallback request, keyboard fallback request, mouse fallback request, SendInput request, click fallback request, value and select and toggle and scroll and focus shapes, and elevation requests

retention of all SG-000027 observation behavior, SG-000018 one-shot and expiry and digest and history behavior, SG-000019 SOFT and STRONG class enforcement, SG-000020 trust and revoke behavior, and closed P08 registry behavior with no change outside UIA invoke policy
Windows and Ubuntu exact-head qualification with Windows-specific UIA qualification where required
exclude: value setting, text entry, and ValuePattern actuation of any kind
selection and SelectionPattern actuation of any kind
toggle and TogglePattern actuation of any kind
scroll and ScrollPattern actuation of any kind
focus changes, window focus, and window close
click as a separate generic shape outside typed InvokePattern
keyboard input, mouse input, SendInput, and synthetic input of any kind
coordinate requests and screen-coordinate fallback
screenshots and visual target proposals
elevation, UAC bypass, service installation, privileged desktop access, and secure desktop input
clipboard read and clipboard write
arbitrary process commands, process spawn, process injection, and process termination
raw Win32 command execution and PowerShell execution
unrestricted process memory introspection
password, credential, and Windows Hello material exposure
observation or control of protected Cotra approval surfaces
persistent approval reuse across operations
approval delegation to remote or MCP callers
caller-supplied approval boolean and caller-supplied approval material
generic network fetch and socket authority

authority_delta.filesystem: No new filesystem authority. Invoke reads live element metadata through the existing observation registry and performs no file read or write.
authority_delta.process: No new process launch, injection, or termination authority. The existing SG-000027 read-only process identity is reused for binding only, and the existing SG-000010 whoami-only spawn boundary is unchanged.
authority_delta.network: None. UIA invoke is strictly local with no egress, and no fetch, socket, or tunnel authority is added.
authority_delta.browser: None. The closed P08 structured-browser registry is unchanged, and no browser launch, attachment, navigation, download, or upload authority is added.
authority_delta.ui_input: One narrow structured UI Automation actuation shape is newly added: uia.element/invoke on exact typed eligible elements with InvokePattern support and enabled state only. No generic click, no focus change, no keyboard, no pointer, no coordinate, no synthetic-input, and no other UIA pattern authority is added.
authority_delta.secrets: No password, credential, Windows Hello, cookie, token, or session material enters prompts, records, history, logs, MCP responses, snapshots, or evidence packets. Password and secret bearing elements are denied as invoke targets.
authority_delta.approval: One fresh per-action SOFT approval is required for uia.element/invoke with exact digest binding over the complete invoke binding set, one-shot consumption, nonce, and expiry. No persistent reuse, no remote delegation, and no caller-supplied approval boolean is introduced.
authority_delta.privileged: None. No elevation, UAC bypass, service installation, privileged desktop access, or secure desktop input is added.

invariants: Invoke binds exact server-derived process identity and never caller-provided process claims
Invoke binds exact typed window identity with handle, generations, session, desktop, workspace, and policy revision
Invoke binds exact typed element identity with runtime identity, tree generation, control type, workspace, and policy revision
Only Button, Hyperlink, MenuItem, and SplitButton elements with Invoke pattern support and enabled state are eligible
Every invoke carries fresh SOFT approval with exact digest binding and one-shot consumption
Stale, replaced, reused, foreign, wrong-session, wrong-desktop, role-changed, pattern-changed, disabled, protected-surface, and policy-drifted targets fail closed without silent retargeting
Protected Cotra approval and security surfaces are never invoke targets
Invoke failure never falls back to mouse, keyboard, SendInput, coordinates, screenshots, or elevation
A missing or denied UIA element never becomes coordinate authority
STRONG enforcement, one-shot, expiry, digest, workspace, and policy bindings are not weakened

acceptance.claim: Tests prove invoke binds server-derived process identity with PID, executable digest, creation generation, session, workspace, and policy revision, and that fake process identity, PID reuse, stale processes, restarted processes, and wrong executable identity fail closed before approval.

Tests prove invoke binds exact window identity with owning process, handle, process generation, window generation, session, desktop, workspace, and policy revision, and that stale HWNDs, reused handles, wrong process and window pairings, foreign windows, wrong sessions, and wrong desktops fail closed without retargeting.

Tests prove invoke binds exact element identity with owning window, runtime identity, tree generation, control type, supported patterns, workspace, and policy revision, and that disappeared, replaced, role-changed, generation-changed, wrong runtime identity, and policy-drifted elements fail closed.

Tests prove only Button, Hyperlink, MenuItem, and SplitButton elements with Invoke pattern support and enabled state actuate, and that other control types, unsupported patterns, disabled elements, password and secret elements, and protected Cotra surfaces are denied.

Tests prove every invoke requires fresh SOFT approval with exact digest binding over workspace, policy revision, process, window, element, generations, control type, and action material, and that missing, stale, reused, and digest-mismatched approvals fail closed with no caller-supplied approval boolean accepted.

Tests prove immediate pre-actuation revalidation denies process drift, window drift, element drift, state drift, protected-surface drift, workspace drift, and policy-revision drift without silent retargeting and without coordinate, keyboard, mouse, SendInput, click, value, select, toggle, scroll, focus, screenshot, clipboard, network, or elevation fallback.

Tests prove caller-supplied PID, HWND, runtime id, selector, xpath, coordinate, approval material, secret fields, and widening fields are rejected as malformed or denied, and that value, select, toggle, scroll, focus, keyboard, mouse, SendInput, coordinate, screenshot, clipboard, network, spawn, inject, terminate, and elevation shapes remain denied.
Tests prove the agent cannot satisfy invoke through MCP tools, synthetic input, coordinate proposals, screenshots, child processes, approval forgery, trust forgery, or replayed prior approvals.
Tests prove replay, expiry, digest mismatch, revision drift, trust-revision drift, and double-consumption protections remain enforced for both approval classes.

Tests prove all SG-000027 observation regressions, P06 approval flows, SG-000018 through SG-000020 regressions, and the closed P08 registry behavior still pass with digests unchanged outside UIA invoke labeling.

Tests prove personal-profile-style widening, arbitrary DevTools or CDP, browser scripting, credential stores, clipboard access, screenshots, coordinates, visual proposals, and network egress remain unreachable through UIA invoke.

Windows-specific qualification proves structured invoke binding against real Windows process identity where required without fabricating interactive desktop evidence, and headless invoke limits are recorded honestly with unavailable-path fail-closed.

Exact-head Windows and Ubuntu Rust, Node, Governance, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, exact-diff security review, manual review of excluded security-sensitive files, and zero unresolved blocking review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.p09_actuation: Value, select, toggle, and scroll patterns with their own approval binding and stale-target revalidation remain successor work and must build on this invoke identity without weakening STRONG enforcement, one-shot, expiry, or digest binding.
successor_requirements.p09_exit: COTRA-P09 exits when Cotra windows are protected, structured action is preferred, and expected process and window identity is enforced, which SG-000027 observation plus SG-000028 invoke plus value, select, toggle, and scroll successors must jointly satisfy.
successor_requirements.p10_boundary: Coordinate and synthetic-input fallback remains P10 work. A missing or denied UIA element must never silently grant coordinate authority.

done_when: Structured Windows UI Automation InvokePattern actuation on exact typed eligible elements is specified with server-derived process binding, typed window and element binding, Invoke eligibility, fresh SOFT digest-bound approval, immediate stale-target revalidation, protected-surface exclusion, no fallback authority, and no new coordinate, synthetic-input, screenshot, clipboard, network, or elevation authority.
